note: validateBillOfSale(d) returns only { completenessClass, odometerExempt, stateRuleKnown } (no rules array, no flags), so this is a SPLIT engine: the oracle pins detectFlaggedIssues(state) as expected.flaggedIssues with flagsArgs ["state"], mirroring form-app.js's `detectFlaggedIssues(state)`. Classification is first-match: riskIndicated (odometer status not-actual or exceeds-mechanical-limits, an invalid VIN, an outstanding lien, sellerHoldsTitle 'no', or a branded title: salvage/rebuilt/flood/lemon/junk) -> 'risk-flagged'; incompleteIndicated (missing party details, signatures, sale or vehicle details, required odometer items, an unsigned title, or a state-required notarization) -> 'incomplete'; else 'complete'. The odometer disclosure is exempt per 49 CFR 580.17: GVWR over 16,000 lb, not self-propelled, model year 2010 or earlier and sale year at least 10 later, or model year 2011 or later and sale year at least 20 later. Deadline flags (release of liability, buyer title) read the wall clock, which test-personas freezes at 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z. Flags are stable-sorted high > medium > low in insertion order within a tier. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas united-states-vehicle-bill-of-sale --update

personas.name: Risk-flagged Florida sale: odometer discrepancy and late filings
personas.description: A 2019 Chevrolet Silverado sold in Florida on 2026-06-15 for $27,000. The seller certified that the odometer reading (131,500 miles) is NOT the actual mileage, which must be flagged to the buyer. The seller filed the Notice of Sale 45 days after the sale (limit 30) and the buyer applied to title 35 days after the sale. Everything else is complete. Expect class risk-flagged, an odometer-discrepancy flag, a late release-of-liability flag, a late buyer-title flag, the FL rule and the disclaimer.

flaggedIssues.description: The seller certified: NOT the actual mileage (warning: odometer discrepancy). The buyer must be warned that the mileage may not be accurate.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Make sure the buyer reads and acknowledges the warning, and note the discrepancy on the title or disclosure statement. Do not certify the reading as actual if it is not.

flaggedIssues.description: Florida expects Notice of Sale (HSMV 82050 or the title back) within 30 days of the sale; it was filed 15 days late.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Keep the filing receipt; the seller stays exposed to tickets and tolls from the sale date until the notice is on file.

flaggedIssues.description: Florida expects the buyer to apply to title within 30 days of the sale; the application was 5 days late, and late fees may apply.

personas.name: Risk-flagged Ohio sale: lien, bad VIN, rebuilt brand, no notarization
personas.description: A 2013 Ford F-150 sold in Ohio on 2026-08-28 for $14,500. A lien held by First Federal Credit Union is outstanding, the VIN fails the check digit, the title is branded rebuilt, and Ohio requires the title assignment to be notarized but it was not. The odometer disclosure is complete. Expect class risk-flagged with high flags for the lien, VIN, brand, notarization, plus the disclaimer.

flaggedIssues.description: The VIN "1FTFW1ET5DFC10312" looks invalid: the ninth character of a 17-character VIN is a check digit, and it does not match.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Compare the VIN on the vehicle (dashboard and door jamb) with the title and correct any typing mistake before signing.

flaggedIssues.description: A lien held by First Federal Credit Union is outstanding, so the seller cannot deliver a clear title and the buyer takes the vehicle subject to the lien.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Pay off the loan and obtain a signed lien release (or an electronic lien release) from the lienholder before the transfer.

flaggedIssues.description: The title carries a brand: Rebuilt or reconstructed. The brand must be disclosed to the buyer and affects value, insurance, and registration.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Disclose the brand in writing on the bill of sale, and have the buyer confirm the brand before paying.

flaggedIssues.description: Ohio requires the title assignment to be notarized, and notarization is not recorded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Sign the title assignment in front of a notary public (or the agency's authorized agent) with photo identification.

flaggedIssues.description: No seller notice deadline is encoded for Ohio, and no release of liability is recorded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Check whether the state agency offers a notice of sale or release of liability, and keep a signed, dated copy of the bill of sale.
